title: Zum Wohl
desc: Eight people, eight glasses, and one rule
setting: Half past five, everybody standing, and a plate of olives nobody is eating from.

steps.speaker: Petra
steps.en: Would you like a glass of wine?

options.feedback: Gern does the work, and naming what you want saves a second question.

options.en: No, thank you. A water, please.
options.feedback: Nobody asks twice and nobody minds. A water is a glass, and a glass is all this needs.
She will pour you something. But the offer was a small question with a small answer.
The name, and her eyes, and only then the glass. All three or it does not count.
Half of it. The name is not decoration here, it is the part people notice is missing.
Heard here too, and it is the louder one. Zum Wohl is what an apéro in Luzern mostly says, and it is what she just said.

options.es: Nein. Ich habe gedacht, es gibt Abendessen.
options.en: No. I thought there would be dinner.
options.feedback: Every newcomer makes this mistake once. An apéro is a glass and four olives, and it ends at seven.
Then somebody told you, or you learned it the hard way. Either way you are ahead.
Three olives and four nuts. Not half the plate, which is what hunger does to a newcomer.
It is seven, and at seven everybody puts the glass down at the same moment with no signal at all.
It is early. It is also over, and that is the shape of the thing rather than a judgement on it.
An apéro has an end time the way it has a start time. Asking her to stay puts her in an awkward spot.
